name: Lana Del Rey
description:
'''Elizabeth Woolridge Grant''' (born June 21, 1985), known professionally as '''Lana Del Rey''', is an American singer-songwriter. An influential figure in [[alternative pop]] music, [[List of songs recorded by Lana Del Rey|Del Rey's songs]] are noted for their melancholic exploration of romance and glamour, with frequent references to pop culture and 1950s–1970s [[Americana]]. She is widely considered one of the most influential singer-songwriters of the 21st century. 

Del Rey grew up in [[upstate New York]] and moved to [[Manhattan]] in 2005 to pursue a music career. After signing with [[Polydor]] and [[Interscope]], she released her first major-label album, ''[[Born to Die]]'' (2012), which featured a cinematic, [[hip-hop]]-inflected sound and  garnered a [[cult following]]. It holds the record for the [[Billboard 200#Most weeks on the chart|longest charting]] album by a woman in the history of the US [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]]. She explored [[psychedelic music|psychedelic]], [[orchestral pop|orchestral]], and [[folk music|folk]] genres on her next albums ''[[Ultraviolence (album)|Ultraviolence]]'' (2014), ''[[Honeymoon (Lana Del Rey album)|Honeymoon]]'' (2015), and ''[[Lust for Life (Lana Del Rey album)|Lust for Life]]'' (2017). [[Rolling Stone|''Rolling Stone'']] ranked her sixth album, ''[[Norman Fucking Rockwell!]]'' (2019), among the [[Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Albums of All Time|500 greatest albums]], while her subsequent albums ''[[Chemtrails Over the Country Club]]'' (2021), ''[[Blue Banisters]]'' (2021), and ''[[Did You Know That There's a Tunnel Under Ocean Blvd]]'' (2023) received further critical acclaim. The latter's single, "[[A&W (song)|A&W]]", was ranked among the [[Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Songs of All Time|500 greatest songs]] by ''Rolling Stone''.

Del Rey is the recipient of [[List of awards and nominations received by Lana Del Rey|various accolades]], including an [[MTV Video Music Award]], three [[MTV Europe Music Award]]s, two [[Brit Award]]s, and two [[Billboard Women in Music|''Billboard'' Women in Music]] awards, in addition to nominations for 11 [[Grammy Award]]s. For her contributions to visual media soundtracks, she received a [[Satellite Award]] and nominations for two [[Critics' Choice Movie Awards]] and a [[Golden Globe Award]]. She also wrote and directed the musical short film ''[[Tropico (2013 film)|Tropico]]'' (2013). In 2020, Del Rey published the poetry and photography collection ''[[Violet Bent Backwards over the Grass]]''.
